% 02.09.2025 CRL.M.(BAIL) 1828/2025 (grant of interim bail)

1. Through the present application, the petitioner seeks grant of interim bail in FIR No.251/2024 under Sections 376/323/313/506/509 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 read with Section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 registered at PS - Jamia Nagar.

It is further alleged that despite intervention by family members, the petitioner continued to sexually exploit the victim by threats of blackmail, eventually solemnising marriage with her on 22.12.2023.
Subsequent matrimonial discord culminated in the lodging of the present FIR.
The petitioner has been in custody since 23.07.2024 and the chargesheet has already been filed.

3. During the proceedings, it has been brought to the notice of the Court that the victim, who is present along with her mother and counsel, has expressed willingness to amicably settle the matter with the petitioner.

sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the FIR is a product of matrimonial discord.
It is contended that the petitioner and the victim are legally married, and therefore, the allegations of rape are untenable in law when the subsisting marital relationship is admitted.
5. It is further submitted that the victim herself has now indicated a willingness to explore settlement, which demonstrates that the dispute is essentially matrimonial in nature.
The petitioner undertakes not to misuse the liberty of bail, not to influence witnesses, and to abide by any conditions imposed by this Court.

6. It has also been informed by learned counsel for the petitioner that he needs four weeks' time to move this Court for filing petition for quashing of the present FIR, in which he is in custody, on the ground of settlement/any other ground.
7. Heard.
Issue notice.
8. Learned APP, appearing on behalf of State on advance notice, accepts notice and vehemently opposes the present application for grant of interim bail.
This is a digitally signed order.

At this stage, the victim (present-in-person in court) along with her mother submits that they have no objection in case the petitioner is released on interim bail.

10. Heard the parties and perused the record.
11.
Having considered the peculiar facts and circumstances, this Court notes that the petitioner has remained in custody since 23.07.2024.
The chargesheet stands filed.

12. The victim's voluntary expression of willingness to settle the matter with the petitioner, recorded in Court on 27.08.2025, constitutes a relevant circumstance to be factored while adjudicating the plea for interim bail.
Further, even today, the victim and her mother (both present in court in person) have expressed their no-objection in case the petitioner is released on interim bail.

13. The fact that both parties are related and had entered into a matrimonial relationship, coupled with the present inclination towards amicable resolution, weighs in favour of granting interim relief.
14. This Court is satisfied that the continued detention of the petitioner, in the backdrop of the victim's present stance is not required.
Accordingly, interim bail is justified in view of these peculiar circumstances.

Therefore, the petitioner is directed to be released on interim bail for a period of four weeks from the date of his release on the following terms and conditions:

d. He shall furnish his complete residential address and keep his mobile number operational at all times.

f. He shall utilize the bail period solely for the purposes as mentioned in his interim bail application, i.e., filing of quashing petition and arranging of documents pursuant thereto.
g. The concerned Jail Superintendent shall hand over to the applicant a written chit recording the exact date of surrender.

15. It is made clear that any observation herein is only for the purpose of deciding this application for extension of interim bail and shall not be construed as an expression on the merits of the case pending trial.
